sam: Ran a focused sweep this morning comparing FlashFusedV2 vs paged-fusion variants across prefill and decode.
sam: Short summary: prefill (long seqs) still prefers paged-fusion for sustained throughput; decode (small-batch, heavy KV hits) shows a visible regression on the fused path.
anya: Numbers? p50/p95 and tokens/sec for decode small batches?
sam: From the replay harness (model=redwood-3b):
sam: decode (batch 1-4) p50/p95: fused_v2 = 24ms / 120ms, paged_fusion = 18ms / 55ms.
sam: large-batch tokens/sec similar, but small-batch fused path drops ~30% throughput.
jordan: Did you capture where time is going (kernel launches, memcpy etc)?
sam: Yep profiled a representative trace. Flame summary:
sam: ```
KernelLaunch::FlashFusedV2  42%
KVPageProbe::aligned_copy   18%
KernelOverhead::setup       14%
DecodeLoop::matmul          12%
Other                       14%
```
sam: Root cause looks like kernel scheduling + KV layout interaction. Fused path has a branch that, when KVpage is present and page alignment mismatches, triggers an extra memcpy path. That extra memcpy + small kernel launch overhead kills small-batch decode.
liyah: So not an algorithmic matmul regression, more perf plumbing. Good.
perf-bot: CI bench snapshot: model=redwood-3b, seq_prefill=1024, seq_decode=32, clients=20
perf-bot: fused_v2 small-decode p95=118ms, paged_fusion p95=52ms
sam: Hypothesis: our continuous-batching heuristics pick fused for throughput, but we don't gate it for small-batch decode where launch overhead dominates.
jordan: Mitigations I propose:
1) heuristic: prefer paged-fusion for decode when batch <= 4 && kv_hit_ratio > 0.6
2) micro-smoothing: delay up to 5ms to form micro-batches for decode
3) allocator tweak: enforce page-aligned KV buffers to avoid memcpy (higher risk)
4) runtime fallback: monitor kernel-launch latency and route to paged variant if above threshold
sam: Quick sim of 1+2 on replay: p95 drops from ~118ms -> ~60ms, tokens/sec improves ~20%. Micro-smoothing adds ~2ms to first token but helps tail.
anya: Latency-sensitive customers (SLO p95 50ms) could be affected by micro-smoothing. Make micro-smoothing opt-in per route.
jordan: Agree. Also add tracing labels (kernel_path, memcpy_count, kv_hit_ratio) so we can verify.
sam: Plan: open PR with config-flagged heuristic + metrics, include replay harness + flame graphs. Rollout canary 48h, then consider allocator change if useful.
liyah: +1. For allocator experiment i'll help design memory churn tests.
sam: Will file ENG-RT-987 as tracking ticket and include links in the PR.
anya: Thanks — please add documentation notes on when paged-fusion is preferred so SREs can tune routes.
sam: Will do. Opening PR and attaching traces now.
jordan: Ping me for review on the heuristic gate and metrics.
sam: Thanks everyone.
